How does this occupation differ from electricians and engineering technologists?

This occupation focuses on repairing, testing, adjusting, and calibrating electrical and electronic systems in commercial and industrial equipment (industrial controls, instruments, transmitters, antennas, and more); electricians focus on installing building electrical systems and code compliance; engineering technologists and technicians focus on design support and test records under engineering supervision. Levels of responsibility and entry requirements differ.

Boundaries

Repair, test, adjust, or install electrical and electronic systems in commercial and industrial equipment under manufacturer procedures and applicable standards, and confirm that equipment and drawing versions match.
Use multimeters, oscilloscopes, and calibration equipment to measure circuits and instruments, recording each raw reading, range, and calibration condition.
Replace or calibrate components and instruments, verify replacement component parameters, and record replaced components and the basis for action.
Perform preventive maintenance and compile repair records, entering deviations, outstanding issues, and recommendations in the equipment register.
Follow electrical safety and work permit systems, performing work on energized, high-voltage, or radiation-related equipment under authorization and procedures.
Retest and submit for confirmation by an authorized role that equipment may resume operation; do not commission it independently beyond your authority.
Work context

Electrical and electronics repairers, commercial and industrial equipment work in factories, pumping stations, communications equipment rooms, or on site, repairing, testing, adjusting, and calibrating specific equipment and circuits.
Workplaces: factory workshops, utility sites, communications equipment rooms, or customer sites.
Main objects: industrial control and instrumentation circuits, transmitters and antennas, and electrical and electronic equipment in facilities and production lines.
Handover is required with operations, engineering, instrumentation and control, and supplier personnel.
Working hours: most work full time; night shifts, rotating shifts, and emergency repair overtime may be required to support production or facility operation.
Risks mainly arise from energized and stored-energy states, radiation-related equipment, and working postures.
Tools and materials: instruments and calibration equipment, manufacturer manuals and circuit diagrams, equipment registers, and work order systems.

Safety boundaries: work on energized, high-voltage, or radiation-related equipment and equipment commissioning may be performed only by trained and authorized personnel under applicable regulations and employer procedures.

Install, adjust, or maintain various electrical and electronic equipment, mainly stationary equipment and facilities.
Covers several paths, with responsibility centered on equipment availability rather than a focus on industrial controls and instruments.

Electrical and electronics installers and repairers, transportation equipment
Install, inspect, test, and repair electrical and electronic systems on transportation equipment.
The objects are transportation equipment, subject to corresponding inspection and operating rules.

Electrical and electronics repairers, powerhouse, substation, and relay
Maintain and repair power facilities and protective devices, subject to power safety procedures and work permits.
The goal is to obtain qualifications for power operations and acquire methods for maintaining protective devices.
Electricians
Responsible for installing, inspecting, and repairing electrical systems in buildings and facilities, working according to local electrical codes and permits.
The goal is to obtain electrical installation qualifications and move into building and facility electrical work.
Industrial machinery mechanics
Maintain machinery itself and transmission systems, focusing on mechanics rather than control systems.
The aim is to combine mechanical and electrical skills and develop toward comprehensive equipment maintenance roles.
Electrical and electronic engineering technologists and technicians
Provide engineering inputs and test records, usually under an engineer’s supervision, without independently approving designs.
The aim is to develop capabilities in engineering drawings, test criteria, and recordkeeping and move toward technical support roles.

subject.summary: Under U.S. O*NET-SOC 49-2094.00, repair, test, adjust, or install commercial and industrial electronic equipment such as industrial controls, instruments, transmitters, and antennas: read drawings and manuals, measure circuits and instruments with instruments, replace or calibrate components, perform preventive maintenance and keep records, then retest and submit for confirmation by an authorized role that equipment may resume operation.
